note: The GAP registry. Vocabulary fixed by Justin 2026-08-08: a STANDARD is a rule we enforce; a SURFACE is a place enforcement can act; a MOMENT is when a surface acts; a FINGERPRINT is a standard's recorded mapping of surfaces to moments plus what its violations look like; a GAP is a recorded FAILURE-SHAPE — the way a violation slipped past a fingerprint. A gap is evidence about fingerprints, not about one standard: it is swept against EVERY fingerprinted standard so one failure upgrades every standard sharing the hole-shape. A sweep records the population it ran against, so adding a fingerprint STALES every sweep and forces the new standard to be checked against every known shape. See scripts/lint-enforcement-gap-records.mjs.

gaps.shapeDescription: The moment IS covered. A live surface sits there, its stated population plausibly covers the violation, and the violation passes anyway — and the surface records no per-decision verdict, so nobody can distinguish 'the rule fired and was overridden' from 'it never fired' from 'it fired and judged wrongly'. The coverage claim becomes unfalsifiable in exactly the cases that matter, and the failure is invisible rather than merely unprevented. A fingerprint has this shape when it names a surface that leaves no trace of what it decided.

evaded.how: Five tone-gate rules classified `blocking` sit at exactly this moment — B15_CONTEXT_DEATH_STOP, B16_UNVERIFIED_WALL, B17_FALSE_BLOCKER, B18_AUTONOMY_STOP, B19_PARKED_ON_USER. B16's population ('telling the user a path is blocked without evidence the agent inventoried what it already has') plausibly covers reporting a peer agent's dead channel as an external blocker and waiting. The gate was demonstrably live — it held one of my own messages the same day for an unrelated leak. The message went out regardless. Nothing on disk records which of the five were evaluated or what each returned: the advisory log captures the DETERMINISTIC preflight layer only (`advisories: []`, `action: "clean"`), never the rule-level verdicts.

sweep.method: Read each fingerprinted standard's declared surfaces and ask: does this surface leave a per-decision record a later reader can audit, or only an outcome?
fingerprintPopulation: One Failure Teaches Every Guard — Record the Shape, Sweep It Everywhere

unmatched.why: Both declared surfaces are build-time checks whose every decision is a visible outcome — a failing build names the offending id, a passing run prints its counts, and the shrink-only baseline file is a durable per-id record in version control. The residual, named honestly: a PASSING lint records that it passed, not which ids it examined, so a matcher that silently stopped seeing a population would look identical to a clean corpus. That is a weaker form of this shape and it is why the script refuses to report clean when it parses zero ids.

unmatched.standard: One Failure Teaches Every Guard — Record the Shape, Sweep It Everywhere
unmatched.why: Its single declared surface is a build-time lint whose every decision surfaces as a visible outcome: a failure names the gap, the standard and the rule that refused it, and a pass prints the gap count plus the population size it swept against. The same weaker residual as Deferral = Deletion applies and is not hidden: a PASSING run records that it passed, not the identity of every record it examined — so a matcher that silently stopped seeing gaps would look like a clean registry. That is why the script refuses to report clean when it parses zero articles or finds no gaps array.

VACUOUS UNMATCH, and the distinction matters: this standard's fingerprint is `none` — it cites NO surface — so a shape about how a surface behaves cannot apply to it. That is NOT reassurance. A standard with no surface is in a WORSE condition than one whose surface leaves no trace, and that condition is already recorded on the article itself as an honest `none` with a dated countdown. Marking it unmatched here records that the question was asked and why the answer is empty, rather than letting a vacuous pass read as a clean one.

The strongest unmatch in the registry for this shape. Its surface's decision is not merely logged — the canonical audit report at docs/audits/<slug>.md IS the per-decision record, versioned, content-addressed, and re-checked against the stamp by both the commit gate and CI. A reader can reconstruct which rounds were run, what each found, and why the stamp was granted or refused. That is the durable verdict trace whose ABSENCE at the outbound surface defines this shape.

gaps.shapeDescription: A standard records WHAT it demands and often WHICH guard enforces it, but never WHICH MOMENT that guard acts at. A hole at the decisive moment is then structurally invisible: no surface, no reviewer and no build can detect it, because the axis on which the hole exists was never written down. The standard passes every existence check while being unguarded where its violations actually occur. This is the shape that made GAP-watched-but-unauditable invisible for a night rather than merely real.

evaded.standard: *all of them* — no standard carried a fingerprint
evaded.how: This shape has no single victim: it evaded every fingerprint by ensuring none existed. It is recorded as a gap rather than a missing feature because it is a failure-shape a fingerprint can HAVE — a fingerprint that names surfaces without moments reproduces it exactly, which is why the lint's moment set is closed and an unrecognised moment fails rather than silently exempting the article.

gaps.shapeDescription: A guard is constructed, enabled, and visible in every inventory while doing nothing — because its arm is unreachable, because another component releases the precondition it waits on, or because the thing it guards is absent. Existence checks and status surfaces report it identically to a working guard, and an injection test against it produces SILENCE, which reads exactly like a clean pass. A fingerprint has this shape when it cites a surface for which no case is known where that surface FAILS.

evaded.standard: Verify the State, Not Its Symbol
evaded.how: Three independent instances inside 48 hours, which is why it is a shape and not an anecdote: (1) solo-captain-hold was enabled, constructed and visible in config while silent-standby-relinquish released the lease out from under it — it held nothing and nothing said so; (2) a two-parents diagnostic I wrote COULD NOT FIRE because the extractor feeding it stopped at the first match, so the condition was unreachable before the check ran; (3) 62% of tracked deferral markers referred to nothing, while the guard proving a marker EXISTS worked perfectly. Justin named this shape as the loop's proof case: under the propagation loop the first occurrence would have flagged the other two before they failed.

sweep.method: For each surface a fingerprint declares, ask whether a case is known in THIS repository where that surface fails — a proven negative control, not a plausible one.
fingerprintPopulation: One Failure Teaches Every Guard — Record the Shape, Sweep It Everywhere

matched.why: MATCH, CONFIRMED BY INJECTION — the first thing this loop found, within hours of being built. Deferral = Deletion's fingerprint originally cited two surfaces; only the ci-time one had a proven negative control. The commit-time arm (the orphan-deferral step in scripts/instar-dev-precommit.js) was believed to work because it has been in place a long time, which is exactly the belief this shape defeats. Injection-testing it found worse than unproven: that step reads the trace's converged-spec path, and the Tier-1 path (enforceTier1) exits the gate before Step 5 runs — so for the ENTIRE Tier-1 commit class the surface is UNREACHABLE. A staged Tier-1 change carrying 'is deferred to a follow-up; out of scope today' passed the gate clean. Every commit in this window was Tier 1, so the cited surface had not run once on the work claiming it.
matched.action: DONE 2026-08-08: the commit-time claim was WITHDRAWN from the fingerprint rather than repaired — an honest fingerprint names what actually fires. Making the orphan-deferral check reachable from the Tier-1 path is a separate change to the gate, recorded below rather than smuggled into this one.
matched.residual: The Tier-1 commit class has NO commit-time deferral surface at all. Extending enforceTier1 to run the orphan-deferral check is real work on the gate and is not done here.

matched.why: MATCH — the second one this loop has found, by exactly the same test that caught the first. It cites scripts/write-audit-convergence.mjs as refusing an unearned `converged:` stamp, and that arm has NEVER been injection-tested in this repository. It is believed to work because it has been in place and because its logic reads correctly — which is precisely the belief this shape defeats, and precisely the belief that was wrong about the orphan-deferral arm hours earlier. Until a case is shown where the stamper REFUSES, the citation rests on reading the code rather than on watching it fail.

unmatched.standard: One Failure Teaches Every Guard — Record the Shape, Sweep It Everywhere
unmatched.why: The best-evidenced unmatch in the registry, and the evidence is not a claim: the surface FIRED IN PRODUCTION ON ITS OWN BIRTH. The moment this standard gained a fingerprint, the population grew from 1 to 2 and all three sweeps — including this one — went red, refusing the build until the new standard was checked against every recorded shape. Six arms are injection-proven (staleness, partition, self-contradiction, reasonless verdict, expired unswept gap, and the clean baseline). A guard that has been observed refusing its own author is the opposite of alive-but-inert.
Cites no surface, so there is no guard that could be present-and-inert. The article's own `none` carries the real condition.

Cites no surface — and goes further: it explicitly REFUSES to cite the adjacent self-stop gate as enforcement, on the grounds that capitulation and quitting are different failures. A recorded refusal to cite is the structural opposite of this shape.
